top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic VeloTurk Gran Fondo Cesme's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.

Road-specific control matters at VeloTurk Gran Fondo Cesme. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 56 miles.
60ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At VeloTurk Gran Fondo Cesme, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of VeloTurk Gran Fondo Cesme. Train it until it feels boring.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
56 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at VeloTurk Gran Fondo Cesme. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,363ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
